title: Ronnie Fixes Your Tech
description: Ronnie hosts a call-in tech support hour with the confidence of a man who set up one printer in 2009. Every problem gets one fix: have you tried unplugging it? Barry tries to help. Barry fails.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and tonight we are FIXING things. Got a gadget acting up? A phone, a fridge, a little computer in your pocket? I've got the answers. Lines are open.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, for the record, your qualification here is that you owned a printer once.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: I set up that printer, Barry. <p:0.3> Wirelessly. <p:0.3> Linda, you're on the air. What's the trouble?

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, hi, yeah, it's my new smart fridge. It keeps ordering groceries I never asked for. I've got forty cartons of oat milk in my garage and it will not stop. It just keeps... ordering.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: So the fridge is talking to you. <p:0.3> Linda, that's not a malfunction. That fridge is lonely.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: It's... it's not lonely, it's spending my money.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Talk back to it. Give it a name. Something warm. A fridge that feels heard is a fridge that stops acting out.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Or she could just turn off the auto-ordering in the app.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Or, Linda, and this is the pro move... have you tried unplugging it?

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Unplug the fridge? Wouldn't all my food go bad?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Fresh start, Linda. <p:0.3> Next caller. Steve, talk to me.

lines.speaker: caller-steve
lines.text: Yeah, Ronnie, my phone battery dies by noon every single day. And I take work calls on it, so by lunch I'm just... done. Dead phone, missed calls.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Easy. A battery is like a gas tank, Steve. You want it FULL. So leave it on the charger. All day. All night. Forever. Top off that reserve tank.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, that's... that is genuinely not how lithium batteries work. Constant charging is the thing that wears them out.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Barry, have you ever run out of gas? <p:0.3> No. Because you keep the tank full. Same principle.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That is a completely different... it's not a tank, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And Steve, if that doesn't do it... have you tried unplugging it?

lines.speaker: caller-steve
lines.text: Unplug it? Ronnie, you JUST told me to leave it charging forever. That's the exact opposite.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Both can be true, Steve. <p:0.3> Mildred, you're on Snazzie FM.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Hello, dear. I'm awfully worried. I got hacked. Somebody's been logging into my email, and I'm scared they'll get into my bank account next.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Oh, a hack. A nasty little cough, that one. <p:0.3> Lozenges, Mildred. Warm tea. It'll clear right up.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: No, no, dear, hacked. Like criminals. In my computer.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well now, that's where tonight's sponsor comes in. VaultBox. The password vault the whole family trusts. Store every password in one safe little box.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, VaultBox got breached last week. They lost every password. It was on the news.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And Mildred, don't you worry about the criminals. <p:0.3> Those people? They've got a code of honor.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: A code of honor. <p:0.3> That is EXACTLY what they want you to think.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Most of them. <p:0.3> And if you're still nervous, have you tried unplugging it? The email, I mean. Just unplug the email.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You can't unplug an email, Ronnie. There's no email plug.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: There's always a plug, Barry. <p:0.3> Darnell, you're up.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Ronnie, my car's touchscreen froze solid. And everything runs through it now, so I can't turn on the heat OR the defroster. It's freezing out and I'm driving half-blind.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A touchscreen. <p:0.3> See, THIS is what's wrong with everything. Back in my day, a knob was a knob. You turned it. It did the thing. Now it's all glass and feelings.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Right, but I still can't see out the windshield.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Drive faster, Darnell. Engine heats up, warms the cabin, defrosts the glass. Free heat. It's physics.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Please do not drive faster while you can't see, Darnell.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And if she's still frozen... have you tried unplugging it?

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Unplug it? Ronnie, it's a moving car. How do you unplug a moving car?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Carefully. <p:0.3> Alright, last call of the night. Winston, you're on Snazzie FM.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Yes, hello. It's my medical alert pendant. The one that calls for help if I fall. It keeps beeping a low-battery warning, and I'm frightened it'll fail right when I need it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It keeps beeping. <p:0.3> Winston, I know exactly what to do. There is one true fix.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie. Ronnie, do not. That's the thing that calls the ambulance.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Unplug it, Winston. <p:0.3> A quiet pendant is a working pendant.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: It... it stopped beeping. Oh. It's gone all dark now.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Silence means it's fixed, Winston. <p:0.3> That's how you know.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: We'll be right back. <p:0.3> Assuming Winston still can be.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I'm getting him an ambulance myself. Off-air.
